packs.title: GST 101: Use of English I - Grammar, Concord and Comprehension
packs.subtitle: A practical companion for the compulsory Use of English course every UNIZIK fresher takes
packs.description: Most freshers lose easy GST marks not because English is hard, but because they answer by ear. This pack turns the rules of concord, tense, punctuation and comprehension into short, testable patterns you can apply under exam pressure. It includes a sentence-error drill, a summary-writing method and a 7-day revision plan.

packs.title: GST 102: Use of English II - Essays, Letters and Advanced Comprehension
packs.subtitle: Write the essays, letters and reports that university assessment actually rewards
packs.description: GST 102 moves from sentence rules to whole pieces of writing. This pack gives you reusable structures for argumentative and expository essays, formal letters, reports and minutes, plus a marking-style checklist so you can grade your own drafts before your lecturer does.

packs.title: GST 103: Philosophy and Logic - Arguments, Fallacies and Clear Thinking
packs.subtitle: Learn to tell a real argument from noise, and to build one that survives cross-examination
packs.description: Philosophy and Logic is where many science and management students switch off - until they meet the objective questions. This pack explains validity, soundness, syllogisms and informal fallacies in plain language, with everyday UNIZIK examples and a fallacy-spotting drill.

packs.title: GST 105: Humanities - Art, Literature, Music and the Examined Life
packs.subtitle: A guided tour of the humanities that gives you something real to say in the exam
packs.description: Humanities questions look broad, so students answer with vague generalities. This pack gives you concrete definitions, examples and evaluation language for literature, visual art, music, theatre and philosophy, plus a method for analysing a work you have never seen before.

packs.title: GST 107: Nigerian Peoples and Culture - Diversity, History and Nation-Building
packs.subtitle: The context every Nigerian graduate should be able to explain without slogans
packs.description: This pack organises Nigeria's pre-colonial societies, cultural institutions, colonial experience and post-independence challenges into clear themes you can actually remember. It replaces vague 'unity in diversity' answers with specific examples, dates and arguments.

packs.title: GST 104: History and Philosophy of Science - How Knowledge Actually Grows
packs.subtitle: From observation and falsification to African science and the ethics of discovery
packs.description: This pack explains what makes science different from mere belief, how scientific ideas have changed across history, and how African knowledge systems contributed to medicine, metallurgy and agriculture. It also gives you the vocabulary for ethics-of-science questions.

packs.title: FEG 101: Engineering Mathematics I - Functions, Calculus and Vectors
packs.subtitle: The mathematical toolkit that every first-year engineering course assumes you already have
packs.description: Engineering students fail FEG 101 for two reasons: weak algebra and rushing calculus without understanding limits. This pack rebuilds the algebra foundations, explains differentiation and integration through physical meaning, and drills vector operations with engineering-flavoured worked examples.

packs.title: LAW 101: The Nigerian Legal System - Sources, Courts and Legal Reasoning
packs.subtitle: How law is made, applied and argued in Nigeria, explained for first-year law students
packs.description: LAW 101 is where law students learn that law is a system of sources and reasoning, not a list of rules. This pack covers the sources of Nigerian law, the court hierarchy, the doctrine of precedent, statutory interpretation and the IRAC method, with worked examples you can imitate in tutorials.

packs.title: ARC 101: Introduction to Architecture - Design Thinking, Drawing and Site
packs.subtitle: From the design process to scale drawings, orientation and the language of buildings
packs.description: Architecture freshers meet two demands at once: thinking conceptually and drawing precisely. This pack explains the design process, how to read and produce scale drawings, site and climate considerations, and the vocabulary you need to critique a building intelligently.

packs.title: PHY 101: General Physics I - Mechanics, Matter and Waves
packs.subtitle: Build the physical intuition and problem-solving habits that General Physics rewards
packs.description: This pack treats General Physics as a small number of powerful ideas applied repeatedly. You get a structured method for solving mechanics problems, a clear treatment of simple harmonic motion and waves, and a formula sheet with the conditions under which each formula is valid.

packs.title: CHM 101: General Chemistry I - Atoms, Bonding and Reactions
packs.subtitle: The structure-and-bonding foundations behind every chemistry course you will take
packs.description: CHM 101 rewards students who can move between the microscopic picture and the calculation. This pack connects atomic structure, periodicity, bonding and stoichiometry, then shows how to set up mole calculations that do not collapse under exam pressure.

packs.title: MTH 101: Elementary Mathematics I - Algebra, Trigonometry and Sequences
packs.subtitle: Close the secondary-school gaps that make first-year mathematics feel impossible
packs.description: MTH 101 assumes you already own certain algebraic habits. Many freshers do not, and the course moves fast. This pack rebuilds those habits - factorisation, indices, quadratic theory, trigonometric identities and sequences - with short explanations and worked examples that model good layout.

packs.title: CSC 101: Introduction to Computer Science - Hardware, Data and Algorithms
packs.subtitle: What actually happens inside a computer, and how to think in algorithms
packs.description: CSC 101 is often taught as a tour of parts, but the exam tests understanding. This pack explains the stored-program model, number systems, data representation, operating systems, networks and algorithmic thinking, with worked binary and flowchart exercises.

packs.title: BIO 101: Introduction to Biology - Cells, Genetics and Diversity
packs.subtitle: The organising ideas of life, from the cell to ecosystems
packs.description: BIO 101 covers an enormous syllabus, so the danger is memorising isolated facts. This pack organises the course around four unifying ideas - cells, information, energy and evolution - and gives you diagram-and-label practice for the questions that always appear.

packs.title: ANA 101: Human Anatomy I - Cells, Tissues and the Skeletal System
packs.subtitle: Learn anatomy by systems and relationships rather than by isolated lists
packs.description: Anatomy has a reputation for impossible memorisation. It becomes manageable when you learn structures by relationship, function and clinical relevance. This pack covers anatomical terminology, tissue types, bone structure and the axial and appendicular skeleton, with a revision method built around drawing and recall.

packs.title: BCS 201: Introduction to Pathology - Disease, Injury and Repair
packs.subtitle: The core concepts of disease processes for students entering the clinical sciences
packs.description: Pathology explains what goes wrong and why. This pack introduces cell injury, inflammation, repair, haemodynamics and neoplasia as a connected story, with the vocabulary you need for later clinical courses and a method for describing any pathological process.

packs.title: MED 101: Introduction to Medicine - History Taking, Ethics and Professionalism
packs.subtitle: The human and professional foundations of medical training in Nigeria
packs.description: Medical school begins with learning how to listen. This pack introduces patient history taking, communication, confidentiality, consent and the Nigerian medical code of conduct, along with a practical study routine for a course load that punishes passive reading.

packs.title: PHA 101: Introduction to Pharmacy - Drugs, Dosage Forms and the Pharmacist's Role
packs.subtitle: Orientation to pharmacy practice, drug nomenclature and pharmaceutical calculations
packs.description: This pack orients new pharmacy students to the profession, explains drug nomenclature and dosage forms, and drills the pharmaceutical calculations that catch students out in early assessments, including percentage concentrations, dilutions and dose calculations.

packs.title: NUR 101: Fundamentals of Nursing - Care, Assessment and Safety
packs.subtitle: The first-year foundations of safe, dignified patient care
packs.description: Nursing fundamentals are assessed both in written papers and in the skills laboratory. This pack explains the nursing process, vital signs, infection prevention and patient safety, and includes a skills-practice log you can bring to demonstrations.

packs.title: MLS 101: Introduction to Medical Laboratory Science - Specimens, Safety and Accuracy
packs.subtitle: How laboratory results are produced, and why pre-analytical errors matter
packs.description: Most laboratory errors happen before the sample reaches the analyser. This pack introduces the laboratory disciplines, specimen collection and handling, biosafety, quality control and the meaning of reference ranges, with practical checklists for the teaching laboratory.

packs.title: ACC 101: Introduction to Financial Accounting - Double Entry to Trial Balance
packs.subtitle: Learn the accounting cycle by doing it, one transaction at a time
packs.description: Accounting is a skill, not a set of definitions. This pack walks you through the accounting equation, double entry, books of original entry, the trial balance and simple final accounts, with worked transactions you can replicate on paper.

packs.title: MKT 101: Principles of Marketing - Customers, Value and the Marketing Mix
packs.subtitle: Think like a marketer about real Nigerian markets, not just definitions
packs.description: Marketing is often reduced to advertising, which is like reducing medicine to injections. This pack explains value, exchange, segmentation, positioning and the extended marketing mix, using Nigerian campus and consumer examples you can analyse in assignments.

packs.title: PSY 101: Introduction to Psychology - Mind, Behaviour and Evidence
packs.subtitle: What psychology actually studies, and how to evaluate a claim about behaviour
packs.description: Psychology freshers arrive with strong intuitions and weak methods. This pack introduces the major perspectives, learning and memory, developmental and social psychology, and the research reasoning needed to tell evidence from anecdote.

packs.title: MAC 101: Introduction to Mass Communication - Media, Audiences and Ethics
packs.subtitle: How messages reach millions, and who decides what counts as news
packs.description: Mass communication is studied as a system of institutions, technologies, audiences and effects. This pack covers the communication process, media functions and theories, news values, and the ethical and legal issues Nigerian journalists face.

packs.title: IGB 101: Introduction to Igbo Language and Culture - Sounds, Grammar and Worldview
packs.subtitle: A structured start for students studying Igbo for the first time
packs.description: Students entering Igbo studies vary from native speakers to complete beginners. This pack sets out the sound system, tone, noun classes and basic sentence patterns, and connects language to Igbo worldview through proverbs, naming and festivals, with drills that suit both groups.

packs.title: EDU 101: Foundations of Education - Purpose, History and Practice
packs.subtitle: What education is for, and how schools actually work
packs.description: Education students often memorise definitions without understanding the debates underneath them. This pack covers the meaning and aims of education, major philosophies, the Nigerian education system and the basics of curriculum and assessment.

packs.title: AGR 101: Principles of Agriculture - Soils, Crops and Farming Systems
packs.subtitle: The science behind food production, from soil physics to farm planning
packs.description: This pack introduces agriculture as applied science and business: soil formation and fertility, crop growth and management, animal production basics, farming systems and the realities of extension and markets in Nigeria.

packs.title: VTE 101: Introduction to Vocational and Technical Education - Skills, Safety and Assessment
packs.subtitle: How practical skills are taught, assessed and made employable
packs.description: Vocational education is judged by whether learners can do the work safely and well. This pack explains its philosophy, the workshop environment, competency-based assessment and the link between skills and enterprise.

packs.title: How to Study at University: A First-Semester System That Works
packs.subtitle: Replace secondary-school cramming with a repeatable weekly study routine
packs.description: University rewards independent work, and many freshers keep using a method built for supervised secondary school. This pack sets out a weekly system: preparing before lectures, processing notes after them, and revising in spaced cycles instead of one desperate week.

packs.title: Note-Taking and Lecture Skills: Capture Ideas, Not Sentences
packs.subtitle: A practical note system for fast lecturers, crowded halls and heavy courses
packs.description: Writing every word is impossible and unnecessary. This pack teaches structural note-taking, the Cornell layout, abbreviation systems and a post-lecture consolidation routine that turns messy notes into usable revision material.

packs.title: Exam Preparation and Revision: A Four-Week Plan That Holds Up
packs.subtitle: Plan, practise and manage exam-day pressure without last-minute panic
packs.description: This pack gives you a four-week revision architecture, a way to prioritise courses by risk and weight, and exam-hall technique for multiple-choice, theory and calculation papers. It also covers the practical side: materials, timing and the night before.

packs.title: Time Management for Students: Beat Procrastination Without Hating Yourself
packs.subtitle: Practical systems for a timetable that survives real campus life
packs.description: Most procrastination is not laziness; it is avoidance of ambiguity, fear or exhaustion. This pack explains why we delay, then gives a practical system: fixed commitments, priority tasks, time blocks and honest weekly reviews.

packs.title: Academic Writing and Referencing: Say It Clearly, Cite It Properly
packs.subtitle: Structure, argument and citations for assignments that would otherwise lose marks
packs.description: Marks are lost for the same reasons every semester: no clear argument, weak structure, quotation without citation and padding. This pack covers essay structure, paragraph logic, APA-style citation, paraphrasing and proofreading.

packs.title: Memory and Active Recall: Remember More With Less Rereading
packs.subtitle: How memory actually works, and how to study in line with it
packs.description: Memory is not a recording device. This pack explains encoding, consolidation and retrieval, then converts that into concrete practice: retrieval questions, spaced schedules, flashcards done correctly and techniques for formulas and vocabulary.

packs.title: UNIZIK Fresher Survival Guide: Registration, Campus and First Semester
packs.subtitle: What to do in your first weeks, in the order that actually matters
packs.description: First semester is easier when you know the sequence: documents, registration, course allocation, departmental orientation and the small habits that prevent avoidable problems. This pack is a practical checklist, not a rumour collection.

packs.title: Hostel and Off-Campus Living: Rent, Roommates and Realistic Costs
packs.subtitle: Choose accommodation with your eyes open and live with fewer conflicts
packs.description: Accommodation decisions affect cost, safety, study time and stress. This pack covers comparing hostel and off-campus options, inspecting a lodge before paying, understanding rent and agency fees, and managing shared living without daily conflict.

packs.title: Campus Safety and Scam Awareness: Protect Your Money and Yourself
packs.subtitle: Practical habits against fraud, theft and unsafe situations on and around campus
packs.description: Students lose money to fake agents, fake accommodation, fake scholarship portals and social-engineering calls. This pack covers how common scams work, how to verify before paying, safe meet-up habits and what to do after an incident.

packs.title: Clubs, Leadership and Volunteering: Build Skills Without Losing Your Semester
packs.subtitle: Choose activities that develop you and still leave room for your degree
packs.description: Extracurricular activity can build real skills or quietly consume your study time. This pack helps you choose a small number of commitments deliberately, contribute well, and record what you learn in a way that later helps with internships and job applications.

packs.title: Peer Pressure and Social Life: Keep Your Friends, Keep Your Standards
packs.subtitle: Make your own decisions about money, alcohol, relationships and belonging
packs.description: Freshers face new freedoms and new pressure at the same time. This pack explains how group influence works, gives scripts for refusing without drama, and helps you build friendships that support rather than undermine your goals.

packs.title: Academic Integrity and Exam Rules: Pass Without Cheating
packs.subtitle: What misconduct looks like, why it is punished, and how to protect yourself
packs.description: Misconduct findings can end a programme faster than poor grades. This pack explains plagiarism, collusion, impersonation, exam-hall offences and the reasonable steps that protect you, including how to handle accidental similarity and how to study when you feel unprepared.

packs.title: Student Budgeting and Saving: Make Your Allowance Last the Month
packs.subtitle: A simple budget you can keep on your phone, and rules for spending decisions
packs.description: Running out of money mid-month is usually a planning problem rather than an income problem. This pack shows you how to track spending for one week, build a realistic monthly budget, separate needs from wants, and create a small emergency fund without pretending rice is optional.

packs.title: Side Hustles and Freelancing: Earn Without Damaging Your Degree
packs.subtitle: Find a skill, price it fairly, and get paid without being scammed
packs.description: Many students want income but start with no skill and no plan. This pack helps you choose a realistic hustle, build one service people actually pay for, price it, find your first five clients and avoid the scams that target young freelancers.

packs.title: Scholarships, Grants and Financial Aid: Apply Without Wasting Money
packs.subtitle: Find legitimate opportunities, prepare documents early and write a strong application
packs.description: Scholarship information is scattered and often surrounded by fraud. This pack explains where legitimate opportunities are announced, how to prepare a reusable document pack, how to write a personal statement that does not sound generic, and how to recognise fake portals.

packs.title: CV, Interviews and Internships: Get Your First Real Opportunity
packs.subtitle: Turn a thin CV into a credible application and interview well with little experience
packs.description: Freshers often believe they have nothing to put on a CV. This pack shows how to convert coursework, volunteering and side projects into evidence of skill, structure a one-page CV, prepare for common interview questions and approach internships without waiting for third year.

packs.title: Entrepreneurship for Students: From Idea to First Paying Customer
packs.subtitle: Validate a business idea cheaply before you spend money on it
packs.description: Most student businesses fail because nobody wanted the product, not because the owner lacked passion. This pack teaches problem-first thinking, cheap validation, unit economics and a first-sale plan, with Nigerian campus examples you can test within a week.

packs.title: Word, Excel and PowerPoint: Produce Assignments That Look Professional
packs.subtitle: The practical software skills behind clean reports, data work and presentations
packs.description: A well-formatted report signals care; a spreadsheet that recalculates saves hours; a clear slide deck earns attention. This pack covers the specific features students actually need: styles, table of contents, page numbering, formulas, charts and presentation structure.

packs.title: Google Workspace and Cloud Collaboration: Work Together Without Chaos
packs.subtitle: Shared documents, files and calendars that keep group assignments on track
packs.description: Group work fails when files are scattered across WhatsApp and nobody knows which version is final. This pack explains shared drives, document permissions, comments and suggestions, version history and offline access, plus a simple group workflow.

packs.title: AI Tools for Studying: Use Them Without Cheating Yourself
packs.subtitle: Where AI genuinely helps learning, and where it quietly damages your degree
packs.description: AI tools are useful tutors and dangerous shortcuts. This pack explains what they do well, where they confidently produce wrong answers, how to write prompts that produce checkable output, and how to stay within your department's integrity rules.

packs.title: Cybersecurity and Online Safety: Protect Your Accounts, Data and Future
packs.subtitle: Practical account security, phishing defence and the legal risks of cybercrime
packs.description: Students are targeted because they hold bank details, social accounts and personal data with limited security habits. This pack covers strong authentication, phishing recognition, device hygiene and the Nigerian legal consequences of offences such as identity theft and unauthorised access.

packs.title: Mental Health and Stress: Coping Skills That Actually Help
packs.subtitle: Understand stress, spot warning signs and know when to ask for help
packs.description: First year brings new academic pressure, financial strain and social change at once. This pack explains the stress response, distinguishes normal pressure from warning signs, teaches practical coping skills and sets out how and where to seek help.

packs.title: Nutrition for Students: Eat Well on a Small Budget
packs.subtitle: Affordable meals that support concentration, energy and health
packs.description: Cheap food is not automatically bad food, and expensive food is not automatically balanced. This pack explains the basics of a balanced plate, builds affordable Nigerian meal combinations, and covers hydration, food safety and the effects of caffeine and energy drinks.

packs.title: Sleep, Fitness and Posture: The Physical Habits Behind Good Grades
packs.subtitle: Small daily routines that protect memory, mood and your back
packs.description: Sleep and movement are not luxuries to be traded for study hours - they are part of how learning is consolidated. This pack covers sleep hygiene, a no-equipment exercise routine, posture for long study sessions and recovering after late nights.

packs.title: Sexual Health, Consent and Relationships: Decide With Information
packs.subtitle: Factual, judgement-free guidance on consent, protection and getting care
packs.description: Freshers receive a lot of rumour and very little accurate information. This pack covers consent, contraception and barrier protection, common sexually transmitted infections, testing and where to get confidential care, with no moralising and no shame.

packs.title: ENG 101: Nigerian Literature in English - Texts, Contexts and Close Reading
packs.subtitle: A reading method for the novels, plays and poems on your first-year list
packs.description: First-year literature is not about memorising plots; it is about making defensible claims from evidence. This pack covers the historical shaping of Nigerian literature in English, the shift from cultural nationalism to critique of the nation, and a close-reading method you can apply to any text on the list.

packs.title: IGB 101: Introduction to Igbo Language and Culture
packs.subtitle: Tone, orthography and the cultural knowledge behind the words
packs.description: Igbo is a tonal language and the orthography is only part of the story. This pack covers the sound system, tone marking, the standard orthography, common grammatical patterns, and the cultural concepts that untranslatable words carry - the ground first-year students most often skip.

packs.title: HIS 101: Nigerian History to 1960 - States, Trade and Conquest
packs.subtitle: Chronology, evidence and the arguments historians actually have
packs.description: This pack gives you the chronology first-year history demands, then shows the arguments behind it: pre-colonial state formation, the trans-Saharan and Atlantic trades, the mechanics of colonial conquest, indirect rule, and the nationalist movement up to independence.

packs.title: PHI 101: Introduction to Philosophy and Logic
packs.subtitle: Arguments, fallacies and the questions that do not go away
packs.description: This pack teaches the mechanics of argument first, then the classical divisions of philosophy. It includes validity and soundness, common fallacies, the problem of knowledge, ethics and African philosophy, plus a template for writing a philosophy answer that argues rather than narrates.

packs.title: REL 101: Introduction to the Study of Religion
packs.subtitle: Describe religious traditions accurately before you evaluate them
packs.description: This pack introduces the academic study of religion: key terms, the major traditions present in Nigeria, African Traditional Religion without caricature, and the method of describing before evaluating. It also covers the ethics of studying living communities.

packs.title: MUS 101: Fundamentals of Music Theory - Notation, Scales and Rhythm
packs.subtitle: Read, write and hear the basics before analysis
packs.description: This pack covers staff notation, clefs, note values and metre, major and minor scales, intervals, triads, and the basics of African rhythmic organisation including polyrhythm and the standard pattern. It ends with an ear-training routine you can run without a piano.

packs.title: FAA 101: Foundations of Fine and Applied Arts - Drawing, Colour and Form
packs.subtitle: The studio habits that carry every later course
packs.description: This pack covers observational drawing, proportion and perspective, value and colour theory, composition, and the material differences between drawing, painting, sculpture and design media. It includes a weekly sketchbook routine that builds skill faster than occasional intense sessions.

packs.title: LIN 101: Introduction to Linguistics - Sound, Structure and Meaning
packs.subtitle: Analyse language systematically instead of judging it
packs.description: Linguistics is descriptive, not prescriptive. This pack introduces phonetics and phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics and sociolinguistics, using Nigerian languages and Nigerian English as data - so the examples are close to what you actually hear.

packs.title: MEL 101: Introduction to Modern European Languages
packs.subtitle: French and German foundations: sounds, gender and basic structures
packs.description: This pack covers the first-semester foundations of French and German: pronunciation and silent letters, articles and gender, basic verb conjugation, word order, and the study habits that make a foreign language stick. It also explains how to use a dictionary properly.

packs.title: THA 101: Traditional African Theatre - Festival, Ritual and Performance
packs.subtitle: Read African festival theatre as a complete performance system, not as folklore
packs.description: THA 101 is where the department teaches you that African theatre did not begin with a written script. This pack explains festival theatre as a total performance event - space, audience, music, costume, masquerade and participation - and shows you how to describe a performance you have witnessed with precision instead of vague praise.
